data.text: Fix bug Bbd88c54354 (no trivial-change gate tier) in ddflow. On EVERY ddflow call pass as_agent=fix-trivial. PROBLEM: behavior-preserving changes still pay full cross-family review + whole-suite ci. FIX: add a trivial change classification skipping review+full-ci, still requiring scoped tests + no-behavior-change declaration; do NOT apply to logic changes. grok-4.7/gemini review; scoped tests before merge; merge; complete --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813-Godzila --regression-test. Return sha + status.

evidence.note: CONFIRMED: a committed whitespace-only edit to a tracked path makes git diff -w base...HEAD empty (format-only) and a code edit does not; probed _is_format_or_comment on a branch: x=1 to x = 1 -> True, x = 1 to x = 2 -> False.

ddflow brief --item fix-Bbd88c54354 loaded. Relevant: r-gemini-key-load (load GEMINI_API_KEY before gemini review), the diff-classification lives in docsonly.py and is re-asked by completion.rules and pipeline_diff. No rule forbids a heavier change (verdict complexity was kept flat).

Committed in the worktree: ddflow/services/docsonly.py adds diff_is_trivial + TRIVIAL_EXCUSED_GATES and pipeline_by_diff picks the trivial tier; gates/outcomes.py and pipeline_diff.py thread repo; completion/rules.py skips the reviewer and records the no-behavior-change declaration (v.trivial); testscope.py runs the SCOPED tests for a trivial change. tests/test_trivial_tier.py is the regression test.

data.reason: the review was terminated by SIGTERM before a reviewer finished: nothing was reviewed, which is not a pass

chunk_findings.detail: The comment-only detector treats any changed line whose stripped body begins with `#`, `*`, `--`, `//`, or `/*` as a comment. Code can legitimately begin with several of these, so a logic change is classified as trivial and skips `rubber_duck`, `critic`, and `ci`. Concrete input: a commit to a Python file adding the line `+*a, = range(3)` (valid starred-unpacking assignment). `_is_comment_only` sees body `*a, = range(3)`, which starts with `*`, so it returns `True`; `_is_format_or_comment` then returns `True`; `diff_is_trivial` returns `True`; the behavior change gates are skipped. The same occurs for a C/C++ change adding `+#define BUFSIZE 256`, since the body starts with `#`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/docsonly.py:_COMMENT_LEADS

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test for the trivial tier only asserts that excused gates are absent from `s.pipeline`; it never asserts that the scoped test gate remains. A faulty implementation could return an empty pipeline for a format-only change, and this test would still pass because `TRIVIAL_EXCUSED_GATES` entries would all be absent and `CO.needs_independent_reviewer(...)` would still be false. That misses the explicit requirement that a trivial change “still requiring a scoped test run.”
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_trivial_tier.py:test_a_format_only_change_accepts_the_trivial_tier

chunk_findings.detail: `git diff -w` is treated as proof of a behavior-preserving format change, but `-w` ignores leading whitespace, which is semantic in Python. Given a committed edit that only indents `return 2` into the `if` body (control flow changes, no other tokens change), `ignore_ws.out` is empty, the function returns True, and `pipeline_by_diff` drops `rubber_duck`, `critic`, and `ci`. That is a logic change the trivial tier must not excuse.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/docsonly.py:_is_format_or_comment

chunk_findings.detail: Comment classification both drops real hunk lines and accepts code as comments. A unified-diff content line for a deleted/added source line that itself starts with `++` or `--` starts with `+++` or `---` and is skipped as a header, so a deletion of `--not-a-comment = 1` never sets a non-comment body. Separately, `_COMMENT_LEADS` treats any stripped line starting with `*` or `--` as a comment, so a C change of only `*ptr = 1;` (or Python/other code starting with those prefixes) makes `_is_comment_only` return True and the same review/CI gates are skipped.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/docsonly.py:_is_comment_only

chunk_findings.detail: Uncommitted logic is supposed to fail closed, but only a successful git result does. If `ls-files --others` or `diff HEAD` is not `ok` (missing HEAD, pathspec error, git failure) the function does not return False; it continues to the `base...HEAD` whitespace check. A whitespace-only committed diff plus a failed worktree probe therefore still returns True and excuses cross-family review and whole-suite CI while uncommitted behavior changes are present.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/docsonly.py:_is_format_or_comment

chunk_findings.detail: `_py_ast_equal` treats equal ASTs as proof of no behavior change, but not all Python comments are behavior-neutral. Concrete input: a clean committed diff to `script.py` changes only the first line from `#!/usr/bin/env python3` to `#!/usr/bin/env python2`. `git diff HEAD -- script.py` is empty, `_show` returns both files, and `ast.dump(ast.parse(before)) == ast.dump(ast.parse(after))` because the shebang line is only a comment token. `_is_format_or_comment` therefore returns `True`, and `_trivial_pipeline` drops `rubber_duck`, `critic`, and `ci` for a change that changes how the script is executed. The same bug applies to a PEP 263 coding cookie change in a `.py` file (e.g. `# coding: latin-1` to `# coding: ascii` while a non-ASCII byte remains in a string literal), which `_show` decodes as UTF-8 with replacement and the AST ignores as a comment, although it makes Python reject the file at runtime.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/docsonly.py:_ast_unchanged

chunk_findings.detail: Still holds: the diff shown does not alter `_COMMENT_LEADS`, so any added stripped line beginning with `*`, `--`, `//`, `/*`, or `#` is treated as a comment. A Python logic change adding `*a, = range(3)` still makes `_is_comment_only` return `True`, so the trivial tier drops `rubber_duck`, `critic`, and whole-suite `ci` for behavior-changing code.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/docsonly.py:_COMMENT_LEADS

chunk_findings.detail: `test_a_starred_unpacking_change_is_not_trivial` does not reproduce the starred-unpacking false positive it claims to guard. Changing `"a = range(3)\n"` to `"*a, = range(3)\n"` produces a diff containing the deleted line `-a = range(3)`, whose stripped body does not start with any `_COMMENT_LEADS` prefix, so the original buggy `_is_comment_only` already sets a non-comment body and returns `False`. Thus this regression test passes on the unfixed code for the wrong reason; the actual failing case is an addition-only `+*a, = range(3)` with no non-comment deleted line. The probe does not answer the previous HIGH finding.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_trivial_tier.py:95

chunk_findings.detail: `ast.dump(ast.parse(...))` drops comments, but a Python source encoding cookie is a comment that changes how the interpreter decodes the rest of the file. A committed edit that only inserts `# coding: latin-1` above `s = "é"` (UTF-8 bytes `c3 a9`) leaves the AST identical, `git diff HEAD` empty, and `_ast_unchanged` true, so `diff_is_trivial` returns true and `pipeline_by_diff` drops `rubber_duck`, `critic`, and `ci`. Under the new cookie those bytes are latin-1, so `s` is `"Ã©"` rather than `"é"` — a behavior change the trivial tier must not excuse. `_show` decoding everything as UTF-8 with `"replace"` makes the same hole for two latin-1 sources whose non-UTF-8 bytes collapse to U+FFFD.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/docsonly.py:_py_ast_equal

chunk_findings.detail: The newly added `and not diff_is_trivial(it, cfg, repo, paths)` is evaluated before the existing `and repo is not None` guard just below it. The surrounding function already has a `repo is None` path (that is the case the existing guard exists to handle). For a non-doc task with `repo=None`, the old code would reach that guard and return a verdict, but now `diff_is_trivial` receives `None` as the repository and will fail while trying to inspect git worktree/diff state. The trivial check should be inside a `repo is not None` guard, or `diff_is_trivial` should return `False` for `repo is None`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion/rules.py:233

chunk_findings.detail:
A committed logic change in a PEP 263 encoded Python file is accepted as trivial because `_show` hard-decodes `git show` bytes as UTF-8 with `errors="replace"`; distinct non-UTF-8 bytes collapse to U+FFFD and then `ast.dump` compares equal. Input: HEAD~1 has `main.py` encoded latin-1:
```
# coding: latin-1
import sys
val = "é"
```
HEAD has the same first two lines but `val = "ü"`. Both `0xE9` and `0xFC` are invalid UTF-8, so `_show` returns `val = "�"` for both; `_py_ast_equal` returns `True`, `_ast_unchanged` returns `True`, and `diff_is_trivial` drops `rubber_duck`, `critic`, and `ci` for a behavior-changing string edit.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/docsonly.py:_show / _py_ast_equal

chunk_findings.detail:
The first-two-line shebang check is defeated by `.strip()`. Input: base `main.py` starts `#!/usr/bin/env python3
x=1
` and HEAD starts ` #!/usr/bin/env python3
x=1
`. `splitlines()[0].strip()` is identical for both (`#!/usr/bin/env python3`) and the ASTs are identical, so `_py_ast_equal` returns `True`. The leading space means the file no longer begins with the `#!` magic bytes, so direct execution no longer invokes python3 (it falls back to shell/ENOEXEC); this is a behavior-changing change that the trivial tier incorrectly accepts.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/docsonly.py:_py_ast_equal

chunk_findings.detail: Still holds. A committed change that only edits the shebang from `#!/usr/bin/env python3` to `#!/usr/bin/env python2` produces an empty `git diff HEAD` and AST-equal parses because the shebang is a comment token. `diff_is_trivial` therefore returns `True`, and `testscope.py` now passes that into `_selectable`, making a behavior-changing Python 2/3 interpreter selection run only scoped tests instead of the whole suite.

chunk_findings.detail: This regression test still passes on the unfixed code for the wrong reason. The change from `"a = range(3)\n"` to `"*a, = range(3)\n"` produces a diff containing the deleted line `-a = range(3)`, whose stripped body is not a comment lead, so the original buggy `_is_comment_only` already records a non-comment body and returns `False`; `diff_is_trivial` is therefore already `False`, and the test never fails before the fix. It does not guard the starred-unpacking false positive it claims to guard. To reproduce the bug, the diff must consist only of an added line beginning with `*` (no non-comment deletion).

chunk_findings.detail: A committed latin-1 `.py` edit that only changes a string value is still classified as trivial. Given `# coding: latin-1` unchanged and `s = "é"` (byte `0xE9`) changed to `s = "ñ"` (`0xF1`), `git diff HEAD` is empty, but `_show` does `out_bytes.decode("utf-8", "replace")`, so both sides become the identical text `s = "�"`. `_py_ast_equal` then sees equal ASTs and equal first two lines, `_ast_unchanged` returns True, and `diff_is_trivial` drops `rubber_duck`, `critic`, and `ci` even though under the cookie the values are `"é"` vs `"ñ"`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/docsonly.py:_show

chunk_findings.detail:
The starred-unpacking regression still does not hit the false positive it names. `_worktree_change` rewrites `"a = range(3)
"` to `"*a, = range(3)
"`, so the unified diff always contains the deleted body `-a = range(3)`. That stripped line does not start with `*`, `--`, `//`, `/*`, or `#`, so a comment-only classifier that marks any non-comment added or removed body already returns false before it ever inspects `*a, = range(3)`. The test therefore passes on the unfixed classifier. The case that actually fails is an added-only line such as changing `"# note
"` to `"*a, = range(3)
"` (or inserting `*a, = range(3)` with no non-comment deletion).
